exam.title: Generative AI Leader
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite or technical implementation experience is required. Develop conceptual AI, ML, foundation-model, data, prompting, grounding/RAG, agent/tool, evaluation, Google Cloud offering, secure/responsible AI, use-case portfolio, adoption, measurement and operating-governance fluency.

objective_coverage.objective_group: Techniques to improve gen AI model output (~20%)
Business strategies for a successful gen AI solution (~15%)

review.notes: All four current domains are mapped through business outcome, data/model/layer and offering selection, prompting/grounding/customization/evaluation, agent controls, secure/responsible governance, adoption and measured operations, with three scenarios, eight labs and 40 original checks. All ten URLs are cataloged: eight reachable and O'Reilly plus Udemy automation-blocked; none missing or broken. The 2026 Agent Platform terminology transition is explicit. No proprietary course material, question bank or recalled exam item is used.

findings.title: Exam and study workbook labels differ
findings.evidence: The exam still names Cloud Functions and Customer Engagement Suite; study workbook uses Cloud Run functions and current customer-experience labels.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the exact exam scope with qualified product aliases; do not invent a revision date or treat new names as future scope.
findings.resolution: Preserve the exact exam scope with qualified product aliases; do not invent a revision date or treat new names as future scope.

findings.title: Prompt tuning has a learned-vector meaning
findings.evidence: The Google Research article trains soft input vectors with the base model frozen, distinct from textual prompt design.
findings.recommendation: Explain conceptual differences from prompt engineering, few-shot inference and model/adaptor tuning, without assuming every model supports the technique.
findings.resolution: Explain conceptual differences from prompt engineering, few-shot inference and model/adaptor tuning, without assuming every model supports the technique.

findings.title: Model choice and owned model lifecycle are separate
findings.evidence: Registry manages models and versions; deployment docs distinguish managed APIs, tuned endpoints and imported models that do not automatically update with Garden.
findings.recommendation: Add a lifecycle/evidence table and correct the workbook-inspired Garden/storage ambiguity.
findings.resolution: Add a lifecycle/evidence table and correct the workbook-inspired Garden/storage ambiguity.

findings.title: Data handling cannot be inferred from a free UI or upgrade label
findings.evidence: Current terms distinguish unpaid/paid service treatment, AI Studio account conditions, API billed-project conditions and regional exceptions.
findings.recommendation: Require the actual account/service path and current terms before organizational data use; avoid universal free-versus-enterprise shortcuts.
findings.resolution: Require the actual account/service path and current terms before organizational data use; avoid universal free-versus-enterprise shortcuts.

findings.title: A training restriction does not eliminate retention
findings.evidence: Platform documentation lists abuse monitoring, grounding, request logging, stored interactions and product-specific retention conditions.
findings.recommendation: Separate training use from storage and evaluate enabled features on the selected platform.
findings.resolution: Separate training use from storage and evaluate enabled features on the selected platform.

findings.title: Personal notebooks do not establish enterprise API entitlement
findings.evidence: The enterprise API is preview and requires enterprise setup/licenses, with notebooks represented in a cloud project.
findings.recommendation: Separate workbook personal-browser activity from enterprise API/account/permission boundaries.
findings.resolution: Separate workbook personal-browser activity from enterprise API/account/permission boundaries.

findings.title: Identity and access control must be designed before data ingestion
findings.evidence: Access-control selection occurs at store creation, and identity-provider changes do not automatically update existing stores.
findings.recommendation: Add identity mapping, ACL metadata, ingestion/federation and revocation/migration decisions with proposed live tests.
findings.resolution: Add identity mapping, ACL metadata, ingestion/federation and revocation/migration decisions with proposed live tests.

findings.title: Schema-valid content can be semantically incorrect
findings.evidence: Structured-output documentation requires application value validation and handling of semantically incorrect conforming outputs.
findings.recommendation: Add separate syntax, business-value, permission, approval and replay tests for proposed tool actions.
findings.resolution: Add separate syntax, business-value, permission, approval and replay tests for proposed tool actions.

findings.title: SAIF spans six control areas and the business process
findings.evidence: The original framework covers foundational controls, detection/response, automation, consistency, feedback and business context.
findings.recommendation: Connect these areas to ownership and evidence; do not imply a single filter establishes secure AI.
findings.resolution: Connect these areas to ownership and evidence; do not imply a single filter establishes secure AI.

blog_intake.value: Clarify learned soft prompts versus manually engineered text.
blog_intake.limits: Full historical research article read; do not infer current model support or benchmark performance.

blog_intake.value: Connect six security control areas to business ownership and evidence.
blog_intake.limits: Full origin article read; linked PDFs not reviewed and historical product claims not treated as current.

blog_intake.value: Preserve developer platform versus employee app distinction.
blog_intake.limits: Full article read in preceding same-session CDL review; no universal feature or security guarantee.

local_validation.execution_boundary: Exact-user ACL model, twenty synthetic rubric observations and fictional value arithmetic executed in local Python. No Google model, cloud ACL, managed retrieval, provider evaluation, identity proof, real tool action or financial transaction.

limitations: Same-context AI review; independent human review pending.

Eight complete cloud/model labs remain proposed. Only the exact public local Python worksheet executed:27 checks over an exact-user ACL model, twenty invented rubric observations and fictional value assumptions.

No LLM inference, prompt experiment, embeddings, managed retrieval, cloud authorization, connector synchronization, model deployment, notebook API, budget, real customer data or external tool/financial action executed.

ACL examples assume trusted identity/current metadata and omit groups, inheritance, provider IAM and concurrent updates. Twenty synthetic observations are not model results; two small-slice observations do not establish statistical reliability.
Capacity value is not realized cash savings. Break-even arithmetic depends on fixed review/rework and stated assumptions.

The study PDF text extractor reported malformed numeric graphics operands (0.00-10); extracted text was read across all eleven pages, but image/diagram completeness was not independently established. Actual PDF bytes/hashes retained.

Paid OReilly/Udemy metadata could not be reverified. Skills duration details and sample-form content were not fully exposed. Public provider outlines were inspected, not paid lessons, labs, practice questions or recalled exam content.
Privacy, licensing, preview APIs, editions, model methods and retention vary by platform/version/configuration; conceptual source review does not validate a specific deployment or contract.
